convert.note: tools/convert/: the converting kit (legacy classes and lock.css to modules) and where it reads markup.

pageParity.note: tools/ci/page-parity.mjs: a page module's comp against its screen file, markup normalised. Attribute differences the modules write on purpose, which the computed-style round check proves change nothing:

tolerate.why: the stage writes the platform on its chrome on every platform (modules read it as a context); the hand-written mobile screens left it off
the keybox writes its date variant always; the generic state pages' hand-written keyboxes left the printed default off. Nothing styles printed (only hand: the handwriting), so it changes nothing

the keybox marks its value as the date hook always; the generic state pages' hand-written keyboxes left it off. Only the runtime reads it, scoped to the recorder and the kept recording; nothing styles it

the stage writes it on its caption on every platform. Not neutral: a tablet or desktop caption takes its stage's width (834, 1440), as stage.css intends, where the hand-written screens left a 390 column under a wider stage. Accepted 2026-10-14 (reference comps only; the website hides captions)

styleDiff.note: tools/ci/style-diff.mjs: the computed style and box of every element, base against branch, per round. The website preview also at 1920, where its gutter changes.

ignore.note: The prototypes' screens not on show: the base builds the quiet navbar's reader when a screen is shown, the modules render it at build time (behaviour round 3, the header); each navbar screen is compared shown.

styleDiff.interactionsNote: Behaviour the screens can't show (behaviour round 2): each scenario's steps run in both builds and the whole page is compared at every snapshot. Targets by text, ARIA or the URL, never by class.

steps.snapshot: hovering an entry kept out of memory

steps.run: const f = document.querySelector('#today textarea[aria-label="Add to today"]'); f.focus(); f.value = 'A new entry from the composer.'; f.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));

steps.wait: [...document.querySelectorAll('#today p')].some(p => p.textContent.trim() === 'A new entry from the composer.')

steps.hover: [...document.querySelectorAll('#today p')].find(p => p.textContent.trim() === 'A new entry from the composer.')

interactions.name: memo playback
interactions.ignoreNote: Screens not on show are left out (a container query cannot match in a hidden screen, v4 D1), and so is the progress clip's rect: its transform is the playback position, the same data as --aj-c-recrow-progress.
interactions.ignorePropsNote: The playback position (--aj-c-recrow-progress) is the clock at the moment of the snapshot: data, different on every run. The playing and played states themselves are still compared.
interactions.shapeNote: Since v4 B6 the memo's waveform is a fixed decorative shape, the same on every run, so its bars and boxes are compared like any other element.

steps.note: a 14-second memo: a snapshot of the whole page takes a few seconds, and the memo must still be playing when it reaches the row and when Stop is clicked (8 seconds raced the end: base against base differed)
the pointer off the rows: it was where Stop and keep sat
the kept row takes focus after keeping at a moment that varies run to run (base against base differed); focus off makes the snapshot the row itself

steps.run: window.__play = HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play; HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play = function () { this.playbackRate = 0.1; return window.__play.call(this); };
steps.note: the first playback at a tenth of its speed: the playing snapshot and the Stop click can't race its end (a slow run's snapshot outlasted the 14-second memo). The page is unchanged; only the test's audio is slowed
normal speed again: the last part plays to the end

steps.run: const r = document.querySelector('#today [role="region"][aria-label$=" content"]'); r.scrollTop = Math.max(0, r.scrollTop - 400);
const r = document.querySelector('#today [role="region"][aria-label$=" content"]'); r.scrollTop = r.scrollHeight;
const f = document.querySelector('#today textarea[aria-label="Add to today"]'); f.focus(); f.value = 'A new line for the companion.'; f.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));

contexts.data-platform: the stage: mobile, tablet, desktop, ios
contexts.data-surface: the shell: notebook, auth (the sign-in spread), account (the signed-out screens)
contexts.data-motion: the shell: arrive (the product shell, the arrival motion scope)
contexts.data-form: the mast: title (the desktop title block). Read only with the value title.
contexts.data-layout: the page: split (the record and its index side by side); the shell: sidebar (a title block as its first column)
contexts.data-clip: the shell: presentation only, a states pack showing many states of one screen
contexts.data-date: the keybox: hand while the masthead's date is written by hand, printed once it is (the glance waits for it)
contexts.data-pos: the booklet: now on the leaf (or the two of a spread) in view, past and next on the rest; a leaf's pictures play as it comes into view

affected.note: Files that never render, besides docs and explore/: a change to them alone captures no screens.
